   ### Practical Trade-off                                                                                                                                              Untitled Session

   Despite being theoretically optimal, BFPRT has a large constant factor (~5× slower than randomized quickselect in                                                    ~\Desktop\crushparser
   practice). It's used when:
                                                                                                                                                                        ◇  via SenseNova
   • You need deterministic guarantees (e.g., real-time systems)                                                                                                          6% (17.4K) $0.00
   • The input is adversarial (e.g., competitive programming)
   • It's a subroutine in linear-time graph algorithms (e.g., finding a minimum spanning tree in O(n·α(n)))                                                             Modified Files ──────────────

   The elegance is in the proof: a recursive algorithm proving its own linear bound by showing its recursion shrinks faster                                             None
   than the work it does.
